#5502. 10 best movies of 2026 so far, according to Letterboxd users

Free daily briefing on global business news.

From The Odyssey to Project Hail Mary, these are the 10 highest-rated 2026 films so far in ScreenCrush's Letterboxd roundup.

Anyone who has stood in a theater lobby scrolling for a reason to pick one ticket over another knows the problem. Studios pour fortunes into convincing you that every release deserves your evening, and trailers dress up forgettable titles as urgent. Friends help, but their tastes won't match yours across every genre. Many moviegoers have turned to a wider circle of strangers who care about the medium as much as they do. Letterboxd has grown into that circle. Viewers log what they watch, assign star scores, and write reviews that nobody pays them to produce. The appeal lies in the motive. These people rate pictures because they love them, and their collective verdict carries a weight that marketing copy cannot buy.

Box office receipts tell part of the story. A blockbuster can dominate opening weekend on the strength of its brand and fade from conversation within a month. A small independent feature can play in a handful of cities, earn a modest sum, and leave its audience pressing it on everyone they know. Ticket sales measure reach and timing. They say little about whether the people who bought those seats walked out satisfied. The gap affects anyone trying to plan a night out, and it can lead an industry to misread what ticket buyers want. Critics cover some of that ground, though their consensus reflects a professional lens. A crowd of devoted amateurs sends a different signal. Countless individual choices about what earned four stars and what deserved two add up to it.

Matt Singer of ScreenCrush set out to learn which 2026 films Letterboxd's users hold in the highest regard. His roundup appeared on Aug. 19, 2026, with the year about two-thirds done. He calls those users the most passionate film fans around and praises the platform as the one social app that hasn't turned toxic. Singer sorted the site's 2026 catalog by average, highest first, and then pruned it. He cut TV miniseries, standup specials, and concert documentaries. He also dropped entries that have screened at festivals such as Berlin or Cannes without reaching cinemas. A small pool of enthusiasts props up the averages for those entries. The cuts let him keep films that played festivals in 2025 and opened in cinemas in 2026, a choice he admits made room for a few personal favorites. The result is his curated list of 10, ordered by the averages posted when he wrote.

Letterboxd users give 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple an average score of 3.82, which beats the mark they gave its predecessor, 28 Years Later, by more than a third of a point. The Sony $SONY sequel earns the final spot in Matt Singer's list with a warmer reception on the site than its forerunner received.

Commercial yardsticks point the opposite way. Singer notes that the follow-up fell short of the earlier film by most measures of success. Letterboxd stands as the exception, the one arena where the newer installment comes out ahead. The split inverts the order the market set between the two films. On the site, the chapter that trailed in the market won more affection from the viewers who watched it.

The rating gap puts the original's average below 3.49, a sizable divide between two chapters of one franchise. Singer jokes that a margin nearer .666 would suit the sequel better, given how the film ends. He leaves the ending unexplained, and the quip lands as a wink for readers who have seen the film.

Sony has a second title on the list, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which keeps setting box-office records. The studio's two entries arrive from opposite ends of the commercial spectrum, one riding record sales and the other carried by its fans.

The Bone Temple sits 0.18 short of four stars, a threshold the original misses by a wider stretch. A sequel that falls behind the first film elsewhere yet outscores it among devoted raters suggests its weaker showing says little about the quality its most committed viewers see in the work. Moviegoers who wrote off the newer chapter on those results skipped the installment Letterboxd raters prefer.

The Furious holds a 3.83 average on Letterboxd, and Matt Singer calls the Hong Kong thriller the one standout in a weak year for action movies. The Lionsgate release sits about a sixth of a point below four stars and edges the list's 10th-place entry by a hundredth of a point. Singer's dim view of the genre's 2026 output gives the score extra weight. A frenetic fight picture faces little competition in a year he found short on worthy brawlers.

The story pairs a man with a journalist. The two set out to expose a child trafficking ring as he hunts for his missing daughter. JeeJa Yanin plays the reporter, Matia, whose search for the lost child pits her against a parade of enemies. Yayan Ruhian plays one of them, an archer in a red tracksuit. Yanin's casting places a woman at the center of the investigation alongside the father. A rescue mission against a criminal network gives the film a reason to keep throwing fresh adversaries at its leads.

Director Tanigaki brings a stunt performer's résumé to the material. He spent years as a choreographer and stuntman, and he has collaborated with Donnie Yen on numerous projects. A filmmaker who learned his craft staging fights and taking falls suits a movie Singer labels frenetic. Behind the camera, that background puts a seasoned fight specialist in charge of the one action film Singer singles out.

Action stands apart from the rest of Singer's list. The other entries include a meta slasher, a debut family drama, a marital comedy, and a buddy movie set in space. Singer names no other title as a bright spot for the genre, which leaves The Furious carrying its banner among Letterboxd's 2026 favorites. Even so, the year's top action release finishes behind horror, comedy, drama, and science fiction films that users scored higher.

Letterboxd users give Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma a 3.91 average, a number Matt Singer calls impressive and reads as evidence that the Mubi release is bound for a huge cult following. Singer describes writer and director Jane Schoenbrun as obsessed with pop-culture fandom, and this film turns that fixation on the slasher genre and the people who adore it. The movie stands as Schoenbrun's third feature, according to the Chicago Sun-Times.

Hannah Einbinder plays a filmmaker whose job is to resurrect a dormant slasher franchise. The filmmaker's blueprint for a bold relaunch depends on the original film's star, a role Gillian Anderson fills. Einbinder's character goes to meet the actor and tries to talk her into signing on. The ensemble extends to Sarah Sherman, Patrick Fischler, Dylan Baker, Eva Victor, and Zach Cherry. The picture nests a movie inside the movie, and its killer goes by Little Death, an allusion to a French expression.

Singer argues the film's self-referential treatment of horror, crowded with nods to countless genre classics, holds irresistible appeal for cinephiles such as Letterboxd's power users. The Chicago Sun-Times reviewer sees a playful send-up of lurid slashers that doubles as a swipe at the pressure to produce original work inside Hollywood's reboot culture. The same review frames the movie as a meticulous fever dream that extends Schoenbrun's exploration of transitioning. Einbinder's assignment to bring back a long-dead horror brand places Hollywood's reboot habit at the center of the plot. Singer's view and the review converge on a film that rewards viewers who catch its many references.

Mubi Fest gave Chicago audiences their first look at the picture in July, according to the Chicago Sun-Times. A story that skewers Hollywood's franchise machine has struck a chord with the viewers most fluent in the classics that machine keeps mining.

Blue Heron, director Sophy Romvari's feature debut, holds a 3.95 average among Letterboxd users. Matt Singer notes that the crowd's verdict echoes the glowing notices critics have handed the film. He adds that users count it among the finest movies of 2026. Janus distributes the drama. Its story follows a young girl whose family uproots from Hungary and resettles in Canada.

Romvari tells that migration through a child's eyes. CBC reports that Sasha, the family's eight-year-old daughter, supplies the story's point of view. The family lands on Vancouver Island in the '90s. Danger mounts there as the eldest son's behavioural problems outgrow what his parents can handle. Romvari drew parts of the narrative from her own upbringing and from Still Processing, an earlier short film she directed.

Memory shapes the film as much as the move does. One critic called Blue Heron a dark horse favourite among many critics at TIFF and an affecting meditation on memory. In that critic's reading, Romvari knots and unknots past and present, and the brother's behaviour nearly destroys the family. Romvari, whose hometown is Victoria, B.C., earned a bachelor's degree in motion picture arts from Capilano University in Vancouver and works out of Toronto.

Blue Heron took home awards from two festivals. Each honor targets filmmakers at the start of their careers. The picture premiered at the Locarno Film Festival, where it claimed the Swatch First Feature Award. At TIFF, it added the Best Canadian Discovery Award, a jury prize.

Romvari's work has drawn comparisons to Aftersun, Charlotte Wells's memory-based debut, according to CBC. Film critic Rachel Ho counts Blue Heron among the year's best films.

Thin margins separate Blue Heron from its neighbors on Singer's list. Romvari's movie outscores Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma by 0.04 points. It trails The Invite, Olivia Wilde's third time behind the camera, by 0.07. Blue Heron stops 0.05 points short of a four-star average. Two earlier features bought Wilde a sliver of separation with these raters and nothing more, a sign that a newcomer can stand beside a seasoned director on Letterboxd.

Olivia Wilde's third feature as a director, the A24 marital comedy The Invite, carries a 4.02 average on Letterboxd and belongs to a club of six 2026 theatrical releases that clear four stars. It crosses that bar by 0.02 points. The five titles above it on the list sit past four stars as well, exceeding the mark by 0.07 to 0.37 points. Blue Heron, the next title down, trails it by 0.07 and misses the line. Every entry below The Invite, down to 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple, falls short of four stars. The film stands at the threshold where the year's most admired work begins, and it is the lone A24 release among the 10.

Wilde's latest repairs her standing with Letterboxd's community after a stumble. Her second film, Don't Worry Darling, holds a 3.13 mark. Singer allows that the score isn't bad, yet he puts it about half a point beneath Booksmart, her debut. The gap leaves Booksmart somewhere near 3.6. The Invite outscores Don't Worry Darling by 0.89, a swing larger than the drop that separated her first two pictures. Singer judges that the new comedy put Wilde back on track and then carried her further.

Wilde plays Angela on screen, too. Seth Rogen portrays her husband, Joe, and the pair share a renovated heritage apartment in San Francisco. Angela invites the couple who live upstairs, Hawk and Piña, to dinner. Edward Norton takes the role of Hawk, a firefighter, and Penélope Cruz appears as Piña, a sexologist. The guests pepper their hosts with rude questions, swap private remarks in Spanish in front of Angela and Joe, and rifle through the couple's rooms and belongings. The setup tests a marriage by bringing in visitors who ignore every boundary a host might expect.

The Invite outpaces both of Wilde's earlier features among Letterboxd raters. No film she has directed has drawn a warmer reception on the platform.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day holds a 4.07 average from Letterboxd users, and the film keeps setting box-office records despite talk that moviegoers have wearied of superheroes. Matt Singer sees no puzzle in the run. Audiences adore the character, he writes, and they adore this movie just as much. In his telling, the ticket sales follow from that devotion.

Singer credits word of mouth for the streak. He judges the buzz around Brand New Day a match for any Marvel release in the past five years or longer. Half a decade of Marvel output sets a demanding benchmark. Enthusiasm on that scale surfaces in two places, the grosses and the Letterboxd average, and here both climb. The fatigue narrative assumes audiences have tired of the genre itself. Singer's read implies something narrower. Viewers keep turning out in force for a superhero picture they believe in.

Tom Holland returns as the web-slinger for the fourth time, according to the Star-Advertiser. His Peter Parker spends the film fighting crime in a world where nobody around him remembers that he is Spider-Man. The setup keeps Parker, stripped of public recognition, at the story's core.

Critical reception arrived with more qualifications than the fan score implies. A Time reviewer credited the film with nudging Marvel toward richer emotional terrain but faulted it for crowding in so much plot machinery and ricocheting emotion that the core story sometimes slips out of focus. The same critic found the computer-generated brawls featuring the Hulk, the Punisher, and Scorpion rote and flat. The overall verdict favored the film. Time's reviewer placed it above most Marvel movies despite those flaws and praised Holland for taking Parker's emotional struggles just seriously enough.

Time's praise for Holland and Singer's point about affection for the character both center on Peter Parker. Neither explanation leans on the action set pieces, which suggests the hero himself, more than the spectacle around him, powers the turnout.

Obsession, a Focus Features horror film made for $750,000, swelled into a half-billion-dollar hit and holds a 4.08 average among Letterboxd users. Its earnings run more than 600 times the cash spent to make it.

Writer and director Curry Barker builds the story around Bear, a young man who makes a supernatural wish that his work crush, Nikki, will fall in love with him. The wish turns Nikki violently obsessive. Singer jokes that the title doubles as a verdict on how Letterboxd users feel about the movie.

Singer contends that no 2026 release has gained more from viewers urging friends and family to see it. CBC News reports that Obsession became the first film since E.T. whose ticket sales climbed from one week to the next across each of its opening three weeks in theaters. Week-over-week growth through that stretch fits the recommendation chain Singer describes, with each wave of moviegoers recruiting the next.

Obsession's half-billion take reaches about 73% of the $684 million that Project Hail Mary has collected. Singer notes that the space adventure cost a couple hundred million dollars, a sum a studio commits only when it expects a picture to connect. Obsession's outlay amounted to less than 1% of that price, yet its box-office tally landed less than $200 million short of Project Hail Mary's. No festival acquisition has ever out-earned Obsession, according to CBC News. Focus Features picked up the film after its premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2025.

Box-office size and Letterboxd warmth part ways around Obsession on Singer's list. Its half-billion gross runs 100 times the $5 million that Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie has taken in, yet the site's users rate that smaller Canadian picture 0.15 point higher. Obsession's score edges Spider-Man: Brand New Day's by a hundredth of a point, lifting a micro-budget chiller above a record-setting Sony $SONY franchise title. Obsession trails Project Hail Mary by 0.24 point, a margin that suggests spending hundreds of times more bought the Amazon $AMZN MGM production little extra goodwill from Letterboxd users.

Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie has grossed $5 million in theaters and carries a 4.23 average from Letterboxd users. Only Project Hail Mary and The Odyssey draw warmer marks from the site's members on Matt Singer's list. Project Hail Mary, the nearer of that pair, sits 0.09 points higher and has pulled in more than 130 times this picture's take. On Letterboxd, a sliver separates the two. At the box office, they occupy different universes.

A gross this size reaches a limited crowd. The score measures the crowd's devotion to what it saw. Few moviegoers bought tickets, yet the ones who did rated the movie alongside the year's biggest hits. Audiences in TIFF's Midnight Madness program picked it for their People's Choice Award.

Neon distributes the picture. Matt Johnson has credited the surprise success of his earlier film, BlackBerry, with helping the project win its green light. One unexpected hit bought the chance to make this one.

The movie captures real encounters with members of the public who have no idea a camera is rolling. Johnson insists nothing seen in the movie is fake. Johnson and McCarrol compare its spirit to Just For Laughs Gags, the Montreal-based hidden-camera program, more than to projects such as Borat. The pair rest the distinction on a single point. Their movie never makes a target of the strangers it records. Comedy built this way asks viewers to laugh with the people on screen.

Two commercial juggernauts trail this oddity among the site's members. The Nirvanna feature outrates Obsession, Focus Features' horror breakout, by 0.15 points despite earning about 1% of that picture's gross. It also sits 0.16 points above Spider-Man: Brand New Day, a franchise release that keeps setting box-office records. Toward the upper reaches of Singer's list, the size of a film's audience reveals little about the warmth of its reception.

Project Hail Mary carries a 4.32 average from Letterboxd users, the second-highest score of any 2026 film on Singer's list, and the space adventure has grossed $684 million. Amazon $AMZN MGM released the picture, with the duo Lord and Miller directing. Singer boils it down to a buddy story set among the stars that pairs Ryan Gosling with a rock.

Gosling plays a scientist who receives encouragement to join an effort to halt a microorganism that is dimming the sun and threatens to kill huge numbers of people on Earth. His character, Ryland Grace, wakes from a coma to find his fellow astronauts dead and the mission left to him. Rocky, another character, reaches the screen as a real puppet, and James Ortiz animates the figure as both actor and puppeteer.

Singer pegs the production budget at a couple hundred million dollars. He argues that no studio sinks that kind of money into a sprawling science fiction epic unless its backers trust viewers to embrace the story. The size of the crowds delighted industry watchers, who had not expected so many moviegoers to show up, according to Singer. Read as $200 million, the estimate amounts to less than a third of what the movie has grossed.

Project Hail Mary trails The Odyssey alone in Letterboxd affection, and a mere 0.05 points divide the two. A margin that thin places a crowd-pleasing blockbuster within a hair of the year's most admired entry. The cushion below runs wider, with 0.09 points separating Project Hail Mary from Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie.

Ticket buyers and the fans who log titles on Letterboxd reached the same verdict on this one. Project Hail Mary shows that a nine-figure bet from Amazon MGM can win over a mass audience and the site's most devoted raters at once.

The Odyssey holds a 4.37 average among Letterboxd users, the highest score of any 2026 release on Matt Singer's list. Singer called the Universal release's finish no shock and wrote that nothing from 2026 so far beats it. His lack of surprise suggests the film arrived carrying expectations as large as its scale, and it met them before the audience Singer calls the most passionate film fans.

Christopher Nolan directed the adaptation. Hoyte van Hoytema, a frequent Nolan collaborator, served as cinematographer. The production filmed across Italy, Greece, Morocco, Iceland, and Scotland. Ellen Mirojnick designed the costumes. Nolan hopes audiences will watch the epic in IMAX. His hope for IMAX screenings frames the film as a theatrical event, and the shoot's sweep across those countries backs that ambition with real-world terrain. Anne Hathaway plays Penelope, the beloved wife of Odysseus. A mob of greedy suitors covets his home, his family, and his title, and Penelope fends them off. The premise places the household's survival in her hands and puts a familiar star at the center of the story's struggle.

Project Hail Mary trails The Odyssey by 0.05 point, a sliver that leaves two big-studio spectacles in a near deadlock at the head of the year. Singer's full list spans 0.55 points from first place to 10th. The Odyssey's margin over its nearest rival amounts to less than a tenth of that spread. Such a narrow band reveals strong agreement among the site's devoted viewers about the best of 2026, across movies of every size.

The Odyssey stands above a field that also holds a Canadian indie, a Mubi slasher pastiche, and a debut drama about a family leaving Hungary for Canada. A studio epic finishing first in that company signals that the site's enthusiasts reward grand-scale filmmaking with the same fervor they bring to small discoveries.

#5501. Former T-Mobile CEO Mike Sievert exits board of directors, wraps up his run at the wireless giant

by Lisa Stiffler on Oct 28, 2026 at 9:51 amOctober 28, 2026 at 10:17 am

Former T-Mobile CEO Mike Sievert is hanging up his magenta hat, leaving the wireless giant’s board of directors and vice chair role effective Nov. 1.

Sievert will also leave the board’s Transaction Committee, according to a federal filing. His departure comes a year after he handed the CEO job to Srini Gopalan.

A company spokesperson said via email that the vice chair role was structured as a one-year term, adding that Sievert has “been a valued strategic advisor throughout the leadership transition, and we’re incredibly grateful for his contributions.”

T-Mobile said in the filing that his departure “is not the result of any disagreement with the Company on any matter relating to its operations, policies or practices.”

Sievert joined T-Mobile in 2012 as executive vice president and chief marketing officer, the same year John Legere became CEO. He later became president and chief operating officer and was mentored by Legere before succeeding him as chief executive in 2020. He served as CEO for about five and a half years.

Sievert was a central figure in T-Mobile’s campaign to brand itself the “Un-carrier.” During his time at the company, T-Mobile grew from fewer than 30 million customers to more than 130 million by September 2025, a period that included its merger with Sprint.

Once the scrappy outsider, Bellevue, Wash.-based T-Mobile currently ranks second among U.S. telecom companies by market capitalization, behind Verizon and ahead of AT&T.

Sievert previously worked at Microsoft, AT&T Wireless, E-Trade, IBM and Procter & Gamble.

#5500. Canton Network and DTCC Bring $30T in Securities to Blockchain

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Canton Network and DTCC are bringing Wall Street closer to blockchain, with $30 trillion in eligible securities now available for tokenization. The launch puts tokenized stocks, exchange-traded funds, and U.S. Treasuries within reach of institutional investors through blockchain infrastructure.

All Systems standby.DTCC × Canton Network.⏱️ pic.twitter.com/ZSI2f3pnWl

This marks a significant step for real-world asset tokenization. DTCC, which sits at the heart of U.S. securities markets, is connecting traditional financial assets with digital infrastructure while retaining existing custody arrangements and investor protections.

Twenty financial firms have signed up to access the service, including JPMorgan, Citi and Morgan Stanley.

The DTCC tokenization service allows eligible participants to create digital representations of securities held at The Depository Trust Company. Registered wallets can transfer these representations around the clock, opening the door to more flexible collateral management and digital asset settlement. The securities remain within DTCC’s custody framework, while their tokenized representations can move through approved blockchain infrastructure.

DTCC’s launch brings those requirements into a live service, although its initial scope remains limited to eligible securities and registered participants.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

Canton Network’s progress shows a much larger opportunity: financial assets are becoming increasingly compatible with blockchain infrastructure, but the industry still needs networks capable of handling transactions quickly and affordably.

Bitcoin has the strongest brand and one of the most established security models in crypto. Its base layer, however, was never designed to provide the same high-throughput execution environment as modern smart-contract networks.

That creates an opening for Bitcoin Layer 2 projects seeking to combine Bitcoin’s monetary foundation with faster transactions and more flexible applications.

Bitcoin Hyper is one project pursuing that approach. Its architecture uses the Solana Virtual Machine to support high-throughput execution and near-instant transaction finality, while its design includes mechanisms for verifying Bitcoin activity and periodically committing Layer 2 state to Bitcoin’s base layer.

The ambition is straightforward: make Bitcoin more useful for payments, decentralized finance, and potentially tokenized assets without abandoning its underlying network.

Solana has demonstrated how fast blockchain execution can feel when transactions settle in fractions of a second. Bitcoin Hyper developers want to bring a similarly responsive experience to Bitcoin-based applications, potentially opening the door to financial products that would otherwise be impractical on the base layer.

For tokenization, that could eventually mean faster transfers, programmable collateral and markets that operate beyond traditional trading hours.

Bitcoin Hyper is drawing attention as its presale approaches the November 26 launch, having raised more than $33.2 million with tokens priced at just $0.0137 each. The project also offers staking rewards of up to 35% APY. With the presale window narrowing and the planned launch approaching, we have less time to enter at the current advertised price before the next stage.

Canton Network and DTCC are showing how established financial infrastructure can bring tokenization into real-world workflows. Bitcoin Layer 2 developers are tackling a different challenge: making Bitcoin more practical for applications that need speed, low transaction costs, and programmable execution.

For Bitcoin, the opportunity extends beyond holding value. A faster execution layer could help connect its established monetary network with a growing market for digital assets.

The challenge is preserving meaningful security guarantees while adding speed and functionality. Bitcoin’s base layer remains the foundation, but its next chapter could depend partly on what developers successfully build above it.

If tokenization becomes a defining feature of financial markets, the networks that combine usable transaction speeds with credible security and interoperability could have a much larger role to play.

There are ghosts in the housing market, writes David Kelly, the chief global strategist at J.P. Morgan Asset Management.

Kelly suggests a number of factors have contributed to the “haunting” of the sector, writes Fortune’s Nick Lichtenberg, such as more than a decade of too-easy money, tariffs, immigration policies that raise the cost of building homes while limiting the number of people who need them, and a Fed whose rate swings hit housing harder than almost anything else.

But contrary to popular opinion that the property market is facing a supply problem, Kelly believes the ghoul in the data lies in demand. He expects U.S. population growth of just 800,000 a year over the next few years. Goldman Sachs’s Pierfrancesco Mei has been looking at workers already displaced from their roles by artificial intelligence, and is seeing signs of a labor market that’s tough to rejoin.

Workers who lose their jobs to AI take about a month longer to find a new role than other displaced workers, Mei notes, in a magnitude comparable to previous technological changes.

Demographics also play a significant part in how difficult it is to find a new role, the research found. Based on analysis of previous technology displacements, Mei wrote that younger workers took about three weeks longer than other displaced workers to return to full-time employment, compared with about five weeks longer for older tech-displaced workers.

Perhaps most notably, Mei highlighted that AI-displaced workers are significantly more likely to leave their prior occupation and industry altogether, but upon reemployment, these workers—especially older ones—have increasingly moved into roles with similar or even higher AI exposure.

Free daily briefing on global business news.

These best-selling Zelda games, the top 20 rows of a 26-entry sales table, span Nintendo hardware from the 1986 NES original to 2023's Tears of the Kingdom

Each slide gives a game's platform, release date and sales figure from the table. The table does not date its sales totals. The figures appear here as the table records them, not as final lifetime counts.

The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild sold 34.51 million copies across the Nintendo Switch and Wii U. That total puts it first in the Zelda sales table compiled by the Nintendo Fandom wiki.

The game launched on March 3, 2017, on two consoles at once: the Switch and the Wii U.

The two versions sold very different amounts. The Switch edition accounts for 32.81 million copies. The Wii U edition accounts for 1.70 million.

The Switch version makes up about 95% of the combined total. It sold more than 19 times as many copies as the Wii U version. The game's first-place standing rests almost entirely on its Switch sales.

The Switch edition would hold first place on its own. Its 32.81 million copies exceed the total for second-place Tears of the Kingdom, a game released only on Switch.

That single version also outsells the next two entries put together. Tears of the Kingdom and Twilight Princess total 30.66 million copies between them. Breath of the Wild's Wii U sales are not needed to clear that mark.

The Wii U edition sits far lower when viewed alone. Its 1.70 million copies would fall below every other row in this selection. That includes A Link to the Past and Four Swords on Game Boy Advance, which occupies the 20th row of the table.

The Wii U figure still tops one other platform split in the table. Twilight Princess sold 1.43 million copies on GameCube, the smaller of its two consoles. Both games came out on a pair of Nintendo systems. In each case, one version accounts for most of the sales.

The table counts both editions of Breath of the Wild as a single entry. It lists the platform split alongside the combined figure. Each console's contribution stays visible as a result. A reader can see both the overall rank and how unevenly the sales divide between the two machines.

The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom sold 21.73 million copies on Nintendo Switch, the second-highest total in the sales table. It arrived on May 12, 2023, as the follow-up to Breath of the Wild.

The sequel's sales figure comes entirely from one console, with no second platform version adding to the count. It is also the most recent release among the table's first 20 rows. The next newest, Skyward Sword HD, came out on Switch on July 16, 2021. That leaves close to two years between the two releases.

Among the four Switch entries in the table's first 20 rows, only Breath of the Wild sold more. Tears of the Kingdom also sold more than twice as many copies as third-place Twilight Princess. No other game in the table's first 20 rows passes 10 million copies.

The game reached both machines within two weeks. The Wii edition launched on November 19, 2006. The GameCube edition followed on December 2, 2006, 13 days later.

Five releases in the table outsell the NES game: Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom, Twilight Princess, Ocarina of Time and the Switch version of Link's Awakening. Ocarina of Time 3D sold 6.44 million copies on the Nintendo 3DS, placing it seventh in the Zelda sales table. The handheld version came out on June 16, 2011.

The 3DS release has its own row, separate from the Nintendo 64 original's 7.60 million. Counted apart, the two versions sit 1.16 million copies from each other. Only two other entries fall between them in the table.

The 3DS edition arrived more than 12 years after the original's November 21, 1998 debut on Nintendo 64. That gap means one game holds two spots in the table, on systems launched more than a decade apart.

The two entries directly above it are a remake and an original. Link's Awakening on Switch, in fifth place, sold 6.63 million, or 0.19 million more. The original Legend of Zelda on NES, in sixth, sold 6.51 million. That is just 0.07 million ahead of Ocarina of Time 3D.

Below it, the margin widens. Phantom Hourglass on Nintendo DS, in eighth, sold 4.76 million. That leaves 1.68 million copies between Ocarina of Time 3D and the next row down.

Ocarina of Time 3D is the best-selling 3DS entry among the 20 rows covered here. A Link Between Worlds, the next 3DS title in the table, sold 4.26 million copies, 2.18 million fewer. Majora's Mask 3D, another 3DS remake, sits further down with 3.46 million.

Together, the three 3DS entries in this selection total 14.16 million copies. Ocarina of Time 3D accounts for about 45% of that combined figure, the largest share of the three.

It is also the highest-placed release on a dedicated handheld among these 20 rows. Every DS, Game Boy, Game Boy Color and Game Boy Advance entry in the selection ranks lower. Of those, Phantom Hourglass comes closest. Switch entries sit outside that comparison, because the Switch also works as a home console.

The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass sold 4.76 million copies on the Nintendo DS, earning it eighth place in the sales table. The handheld game was released on June 23, 2007.

That total makes Phantom Hourglass the best-selling DS game among these 20 entries. The only other DS release in this group is Spirit Tracks, which arrived in December 2009 and sold 2.96 million copies. Phantom Hourglass finished 1.80 million copies ahead of it.

Among releases for Nintendo's handheld-only systems, just one game ranks higher in the table. That game is Ocarina of Time 3D, the 2011 Nintendo 3DS remake, which leads Phantom Hourglass by 1.68 million copies.

Phantom Hourglass also outsold the next 3DS entry in the table. A Link Between Worlds, released in November 2013, sold 4.26 million copies. That leaves it 0.50 million copies behind the DS game.

The DS game sits above several home console entries as well. A Link to the Past on the Super Nintendo sold 4.61 million copies and ranks directly below it, 0.15 million copies back. The Wind Waker on GameCube follows with 4.43 million, a gap of 0.33 million.

Its total tops every Game Boy family release in this selection. That group covers the 1993 Game Boy version of Link's Awakening and the paired Oracle $ORCL of Seasons and Oracle of Ages on Game Boy Color. The group also includes A Link to the Past and Four Swords on Game Boy Advance.

Zelda II: The Adventure of Link on the NES trails the DS game. So does Skyward Sword, in both its Wii original and its Switch HD version. Both versions of Majora's Mask, on Nintendo 64 and 3DS, rank below it too.

In release order, Phantom Hourglass was the first entry in this selection to follow Twilight Princess. The two DS games are the only releases in this group between Twilight Princess in late 2006 and Ocarina of Time 3D in mid-2011.

A Link to the Past sold 4.61 million copies on the Super Nintendo. That total places the 1991 release ninth in the Zelda sales table.

It is the only Super Nintendo game in the table's top 20 rows. Every other entry in that group came out on a different Nintendo console or handheld.

The game launched on November 21, 1991. That was more than five years after the original Legend of Zelda arrived on the NES. It also came out seven years to the day before Ocarina of Time reached the Nintendo 64.

Two later releases sit on either side of its sales figure. Phantom Hourglass, a 2007 Nintendo DS game, ranks one place higher with 4.76 million. The Wind Waker, a 2002 GameCube release, ranks one place lower with 4.43 million. The gap above A Link to the Past is 150,000 copies. The gap below is 180,000.

The two NES games that preceded it also bracket it in the ranking. The 1986 original ranks three places higher, in sixth. Zelda II: The Adventure of Link ranks two places lower, in 11th.

Four games in the table's top 20 rows predate the Nintendo 64. A Link to the Past ranks second among them, behind only the 1986 original. The 1993 Game Boy version of Link's Awakening completes that group in 15th place.

Among the 1990s releases in this selection, only Ocarina of Time outranks it. The 1991 game also places above several later home-console entries. Skyward Sword on Wii, released in 2011, ranks 16th. Majora's Mask, the 2000 Nintendo 64 game, ranks 18th.

A later Game Boy Advance version, A Link to the Past and Four Swords, came out on December 2, 2002. It holds its own, lower row in the table. It reached stores 11 days before The Wind Waker arrived on GameCube.

The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker sold 4.43 million copies on GameCube, which places it 10th in the sales table. Nintendo released it on December 13, 2002.

That total puts it close to the games ranked around it. A Link to the Past on Super Nintendo sits one place higher with 4.61 million, a gap of 0.18 million. Zelda II: The Adventure of Link on NES follows at 4.38 million, just 0.05 million behind. The five games ranked ninth through 13th all fall between 4.15 million and 4.61 million, a spread of 0.46 million.

The Wind Waker also outsold two other home console entries in the table. Majora's Mask, released on Nintendo 64 on April 27, 2000, sold 3.36 million copies, 1.07 million fewer. Skyward Sword, released on Wii on November 18, 2011, sold 3.67 million, 0.76 million below The Wind Waker.

The Wind Waker is the only game in this 20-title selection released solely on GameCube. Twilight Princess also came out on the console nearly four years later, alongside its Wii version. That GameCube edition sold 1.43 million copies. The Wind Waker outsold it on the same hardware by 3.00 million.

The Wind Waker was one of two Zelda releases in the table from December 2002. A Link to the Past and Four Swords reached Game Boy Advance on December 2, 11 days before The Wind Waker. That handheld release sold 1.61 million fewer copies than the GameCube game.

The game's art direction set it apart from Ocarina of Time. The Wind Waker replaced that game's more realistic look with a stylized, cartoon-like Link. Some players pushed back on the change and called it a backwards step. The visual design later earned the game several awards.

Wind Waker HD appears as its own entry in 21st place, just outside this selection. The 4.43 million figure covers the GameCube release alone.

Zelda II: The Adventure of Link sold 4.38 million copies on the Nintendo Entertainment System. That total ranks it 11th in the sales table.

The game was released on January 14, 1987. The sequel reached shelves less than a year after the original Legend of Zelda, which launched the series on the same console.

The two NES entries finished 2.13 million copies apart. The original holds sixth place.

Zelda II is the second-oldest game among the first 20 rows of the table. Only the 1986 original predates it. The next-oldest entry, A Link to the Past on Super Nintendo, came out in November 1991.

The Adventure of Link sits in a close cluster in the middle of the ranking. The Wind Waker on GameCube sold 4.43 million, 50,000 copies more. A Link Between Worlds on Nintendo 3DS sold 4.26 million, or 120,000 fewer.

Those neighbors came out much later. The Wind Waker was released in December 2002. A Link Between Worlds followed in November 2013.

All nine entries ranked below Zelda II in this selection were released after it. Skyward Sword HD, the 2021 Switch release, sold 4.15 million. Oracle $ORCL of Seasons and Oracle of Ages, the 2001 Game Boy Color pair, sold 3.99 million combined.

Majora's Mask, the 2000 Nintendo 64 title, sold 3.36 million. Spirit Tracks, the 2009 Nintendo DS game, sold 2.96 million.

A Link Between Worlds sold 4.26 million copies on the Nintendo 3DS. That total places it 12th in the Zelda sales table. The handheld game came out on November 22, 2013.

Its total sits in a tight cluster near the middle of the selection. It trails Zelda II: The Adventure of Link, the NES follow-up to the original game, by 0.12 million copies. It finishes 0.11 million ahead of Skyward Sword HD, which arrived on Switch in 2021.

Those three neighboring entries come from three different decades. Each also appeared on a different Nintendo platform.

Among games released on Nintendo's dedicated handhelds, only two rank higher in this selection. They are Ocarina of Time 3D on the 3DS and Phantom Hourglass on the DS.

Three 3DS games appear in the table's first 20 rows. Ocarina of Time 3D, released in 2011, leads that group. It finished 2.18 million copies ahead of A Link Between Worlds.

Majora's Mask 3D, released in February 2015, comes third among the 3DS entries with 3.46 million. That puts it 0.80 million behind A Link Between Worlds.

By release date, A Link Between Worlds is the middle of the three 3DS entries. It arrived between the two remakes.

It is also the only one of the three that does not share its name with a Nintendo 64 game in the table. The other two 3DS entries are versions of Nintendo 64 releases that hold their own rows.

Skyward Sword HD sold 4.15 million copies on Nintendo Switch, which places it 13th in the Zelda sales table. The game came out on July 16, 2021.

That date makes it the second-newest game in these 20 rows. Tears of the Kingdom, released in May 2023, is the only entry that arrived later.

Among the Switch releases in this selection, Skyward Sword HD has the lowest total. The others are Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom and the 2019 Link's Awakening remake. Link's Awakening on Switch, the nearest of those three, sold 2.48 million more copies.

Sharing a console did not produce similar results. Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom hold the top two places. The two Switch versions of older games, Link's Awakening and Skyward Sword HD, sit well below them, in fifth and 13th.

The Wii version of Skyward Sword came out on November 18, 2011, and has its own row in the table. The HD release followed about nine years and eight months later. The 4.15 million figure counts Switch sales only and leaves out the Wii total.

The Switch release ranks above the Wii original. Majora's Mask and Link's Awakening follow the same pattern, with each newer version placing higher than the earlier one. Ocarina of Time runs the other way, with the Nintendo 64 original ahead of the 3DS remake.

Skyward Sword HD sits close to its neighbors in the table. A Link Between Worlds on 3DS, one place higher, sold 0.11 million more copies. The combined Oracle $ORCL of Seasons and Oracle of Ages row on Game Boy Color, one place lower, sold 0.16 million fewer.

Oracle $ORCL of Seasons and Oracle of Ages sold 3.99 million copies combined on Game Boy Color. The pair came out on February 27, 2001, and ranks 14th in the sales table.

The source lists both games in a single row. It gives them one platform, one release date and one sales total. It does not split the 3.99 million figure between the two titles.

That missing split limits what the row can show. The table does not reveal which Oracle game sold more. Nor does it show where either title would rank if listed alone.

The joint listing also differs from the other combined totals near the top of the ranking. Breath of the Wild and Twilight Princess carry combined figures too. Those totals add together versions of one game released on two different consoles. The Oracle row instead covers two separately named games on the same handheld, released on the same day.

This is the only Game Boy Color entry among the first 20 rows of the table. Every other handheld entry in that range comes from the original Game Boy, the Game Boy Advance, the DS or the 3DS.

The pair's combined total sits close to its neighbors in the ranking. It is 160,000 copies above Link's Awakening on the original Game Boy, which sold 3.83 million. It is 160,000 copies below Skyward Sword HD on Switch, which sold 4.15 million. Those equal gaps put the Oracle row exactly midway between the two entries.

Link's Awakening on the original Game Boy sold 3.83 million copies, which places it 15th in a 26-entry table of Zelda sales. The handheld game came out on June 6, 1993.

It is the only game for the original Game Boy among the table's first 20 rows. The other handheld entries in that range run on the Game Boy Color, Game Boy Advance, DS and 3DS.

Its release date also makes it one of the older games in this group. Only three games in the first 20 rows came out before it. They are the original Legend of Zelda in 1986, Zelda II: The Adventure of Link in 1987 and A Link to the Past in 1991.

The story begins when Link washes ashore on Koholint Island after a storm. His first task is to recover his sword and shield from the beach.

His larger goal is to gather a set of instruments. Together they let him play a melody that wakes a fish deity. That deity is dreaming the whole of Koholint Island.

The island also carries small references to classic Nintendo characters. One town resident keeps Chompers from Super Mario Bros. as pets.

The 2019 Nintendo Switch remake of the same game sold 6.63 million copies. That is 2.80 million more than the 1993 Game Boy release. A third version, Link's Awakening DX, falls among the six entries outside this selection. In this table, the newer version of the same adventure outsold the Game Boy original.

The Game Boy release sits between two close neighbors in the table. Oracle $ORCL of Seasons and Oracle of Ages sold 3.99 million combined on Game Boy Color, one row above it. Skyward Sword on Wii sold 3.67 million, one row below. Each neighbor's total is 0.16 million away from the Game Boy game's 3.83 million. Those three rows come from three different decades and three different Nintendo platforms.

The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword sold 3.67 million copies on the Wii. That total ranks 16th in the Nintendo Fandom wiki's table of Zelda sales.

The game came out on November 18, 2011. The table lists the Wii as its only platform. No other row among the table's 26 entries is a Wii-only release.

Twilight Princess is the table's other Wii game. It reached the console on November 19, 2006, about five years before Skyward Sword. That release also came out on GameCube. Its Wii version alone sold 7.50 million copies, more than double Skyward Sword's total.

Skyward Sword was the second of two Zelda releases from 2011 in this selection. Ocarina of Time 3D reached the Nintendo 3DS that June.

A Switch version, Skyward Sword HD, followed on July 16, 2021. The table gives it a separate row with 4.15 million copies sold. That puts the newer version 0.48 million copies ahead of the Wii original.

Two other games in this selection show the same pattern. The later versions of Link's Awakening and Majora's Mask both outsold the originals. Ocarina of Time breaks it, with the Nintendo 64 game ahead of its 3DS remake.

Good Game reviewer Bajo described the Wii game's motion controls as hit and miss. Steering a mechanical beetle felt fluid and intuitive to him. In his view, shaking the remote to make the Loftwing flap faster felt clunky and out of control.

Majora's Mask 3D, the Nintendo 3DS version of the 2000 Nintendo 64 game, sold 3.46 million copies. That total places it 17th in the Zelda sales table.

The handheld version came out on February 13, 2015. That was nearly 15 years after Majora's Mask first launched on Nintendo 64 on April 27, 2000.

The 3DS release finished slightly ahead of the original, which sold 3.36 million copies. The gap between the two is 0.10 million copies, or about 100,000. In the table, the two versions sit in neighboring rows.

Majora's Mask 3D is one of three Nintendo 3DS games in the table's first 20 rows. The others are Ocarina of Time 3D, released June 16, 2011, and A Link Between Worlds, released November 22, 2013. A Link Between Worlds sold 4.26 million copies.

Of those three 3DS releases, Majora's Mask 3D posted the lowest total. It was also the last of the three to arrive on the system.

Its result against the original runs the other way from Ocarina of Time 3D. That 3DS remake sold fewer copies than the Nintendo 64 Ocarina of Time. Majora's Mask 3D edged past its Nintendo 64 predecessor instead.

Majora's Mask sold 3.36 million copies on the Nintendo 64. The game came out on April 27, 2000, and ranks 18th in the Zelda sales table.

It arrived on the same console about 17 months after Ocarina of Time. The two are the only Nintendo 64 releases anywhere in the table.

Ocarina of Time sold more than twice as many copies as its follow-up. The gap between the two Nintendo 64 games is 4.24 million copies.

The 3.36 million figure covers the original Nintendo 64 release only. Majora's Mask 3D, the 2015 Nintendo 3DS version, has its own row one place higher, at 3.46 million. The handheld version arrived nearly 15 years after the original and outsold it by 0.10 million copies.

Only two of the 20 rows in this selection sold fewer copies than Majora's Mask. Spirit Tracks on Nintendo DS sold 2.96 million. A Link to the Past and Four Swords on Game Boy Advance sold 2.82 million.

Both of those games came out on handhelds. Every home console entry in the selection sold more than Majora's Mask, which makes it the lowest-selling home console game among these 20 rows.

The Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks sold 2.96 million copies on the Nintendo DS. Released on December 7, 2009, it ranks 19th in the source's 26-entry sales table.

It is one of two Nintendo DS games among the 20 rows covered here. The other, Phantom Hourglass, came out in June 2007 and sold 4.76 million copies. Spirit Tracks arrived about two and a half years later. It trails that earlier handheld entry by 1.80 million copies.

Good Game reports that the story opens with the railway lines acting as enchanted restraints. They keep a demon king locked beneath the ground. When the tracks begin to vanish, Link has to repair them.

That repair work does double duty. Each restored line also contributes to rebuilding the Spirit Tower, which stands at the point where every line meets.

The train matters outside the main quest as well. Optional side-quests have Link ferrying passengers around or carrying cargo between towns. To complete those runs, the player must follow railway rules. That means sounding the horn at certain points and changing speeds.

Some puzzles put Link and a partner character under the player's control at the same time. The DS touch screen handles the coordination. The player sketches a route on it, and the partner follows that path.

The Good Game reviewers also pointed to a drawback. They said the game involves a lot of dead time spent watching the train travel from one point to another. Warp gates offer a shortcut, teleporting the player to different quarters of the map.

The same reviewers noted several elements carried over from the previous game in the series. Beedle's shop returns, as do treasure items. Upgrades for the train parallel the boat upgrades of that earlier entry.

Spirit Tracks takes place about a hundred years after that predecessor, according to Good Game.

A Link to the Past and Four Swords for Game Boy Advance sold 2.82 million copies. That total ranks the handheld release 20th in the Zelda sales table.

The game came out on December 2, 2002. The table gives it a row of its own, separate from A Link to the Past on Super Nintendo. That console version launched on November 21, 1991, and sold 4.61 million copies.

The handheld edition arrived 11 years after the Super Nintendo original. Its sales total sits 1.79 million copies below the earlier version's. The 1991 console release ranks higher of the two.

This is the only Game Boy Advance release among the 20 entries in this selection. Every other handheld entry in the group came out on Game Boy, Game Boy Color, DS or 3DS.

December 2002 brought two Zelda releases on two different Nintendo systems. The Wind Waker reached GameCube on December 13, 2002. That was 11 days after the Game Boy Advance title.

Spirit Tracks on Nintendo DS ranks one place higher, with 2.96 million copies. The gap between the two entries is 0.14 million copies.

#5497. 9 Hidden Technology Challenges That Can Slow Down Business Growth

You're viewing the US website. Looking for the Site edition?

Discover the technology challenges entrepreneurs must address to improve operational efficiency, reduce costs and build a future-ready business.

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

For most entrepreneurs, growth is the ultimate measure of success. Expanding into new markets, acquiring customers, increasing revenue and building stronger teams are often the priorities that dominate strategic discussions.

However, one critical factor frequently receives less attention: the technology infrastructure supporting everyday business operations.

A company might have an excellent product, a growing customer base and an ambitious expansion strategy, yet still struggle to scale because its internal systems cannot keep up with increasing demand.

Technology challenges rarely appear overnight. They develop gradually through outdated software, disconnected applications, inefficient databases, inadequate security measures and technology investments made without a long-term strategy.

These issues may seem manageable during the early stages of business development. But as organizations grow, even minor inefficiencies can become expensive obstacles.

Understanding these hidden challenges is essential for entrepreneurs who want to build businesses capable of sustaining long-term growth.

One of the biggest challenges growing businesses face is their dependence on outdated technology.

Many organizations continue using software and infrastructure implemented years earlier. These systems may still perform their original functions, making replacement or modernization appear unnecessary.

However, maintaining older technology can become increasingly expensive. Outdated systems may require specialized technical support, frequent maintenance, manual workarounds and additional resources to remain compatible with newer applications.

The financial impact extends beyond direct maintenance expenses. Employees may spend additional hours completing routine tasks, departments may struggle to exchange information, and customers may experience slower service.

These inefficiencies reduce productivity and make it harder for companies to respond quickly to changing market conditions.

For business leaders, the important question is not simply whether existing technology still works. It is whether that technology continues to support the organization’s future requirements.

Regular infrastructure assessments can help identify systems that are becoming expensive to maintain or increasingly difficult to integrate with modern business applications.

As businesses expand, they frequently introduce new software to address specific operational requirements.

A sales department might adopt a customer relationship management platform, while the finance team uses separate accounting software. Marketing teams may rely on analytics platforms, and operations departments might introduce project management applications.

Each tool can provide individual benefits. However, problems arise when these systems cannot communicate effectively. Employees may need to enter identical information into multiple applications. Managers might receive conflicting reports, while customer-facing teams struggle to access accurate information.

Consider a growing service company where sales, billing and customer support operate through separate systems. When a customer purchases a service, employees may need to manually transfer details between departments. This increases the possibility of errors and delays.

As transaction volumes increase, these problems become more difficult to manage.

The solution is not necessarily purchasing additional software. Instead, companies should evaluate how existing applications exchange information and whether integration or workflow improvements can eliminate unnecessary manual tasks.

Entrepreneur’s discussion of why businesses can have access to powerful tools and still struggle to make progress highlights the importance of turning technology availability into practical business capabilities.

Entrepreneurs should prioritize connected systems that provide reliable information across departments and simplify daily operations.

Behind most business applications is a database responsible for storing, organizing and retrieving critical information. Customer records, financial transactions, inventory details, employee information and operational reports often depend on database infrastructure.

When businesses are relatively small, database performance may receive little attention. However, as customer activity increases and applications become more complex, limitations in database architecture can begin affecting operations.

Slow queries, inefficient data processing, limited integration capabilities and inadequate capacity planning can create performance bottlenecks. These issues may result in delayed reports, slower applications and additional infrastructure expenses.

Database selection also involves important architectural considerations.

For example, organizations maintaining applications built around SAP SQL Anywhere or SAP Adaptive Server Enterprise may need to evaluate differences in their deployment requirements, workload characteristics, administrative complexity and scalability.

Understanding how different database systems compare can help technical teams assess the suitability of existing platforms before making decisions about application upgrades or infrastructure modernization.

Importantly, replacing a database is not always the best solution. In some cases, performance improvements can be achieved through query optimization, indexing, infrastructure upgrades or improved database administration.

In other situations, changing business requirements may justify a more substantial modernization initiative.

Entrepreneurs do not need to become database specialists. However, they should understand how database reliability, performance and maintenance requirements affect customer experience and business continuity.

Treating data infrastructure as a strategic business asset rather than an isolated technical concern can help organizations avoid costly decisions as they expand.

Businesses are constantly introduced to new technologies promising greater efficiency, improved customer experiences and increased profitability. Artificial intelligence, automation, cloud platforms and advanced analytics all offer meaningful opportunities.

However, adopting technology without clearly defined objectives can create additional complexity instead of delivering measurable improvements.

A company might invest in an expensive automation platform without first examining whether its underlying processes are efficient. Another business might purchase sophisticated analytics software without having employees who can interpret and act on the information.

In both situations, the problem is not necessarily the technology itself. It is the absence of a clear implementation strategy.

Before introducing a new system, business leaders should identify the operational challenge they want to solve. They should also establish measurable success indicators, such as reduced processing time, improved customer response rates, lower operational expenses or increased employee productivity.

A practical approach involves testing new technology within a limited business function before expanding its use across the organization. This allows teams to evaluate effectiveness, identify implementation challenges and determine whether the investment provides sufficient value.

Technology should support business strategy rather than become a substitute for it.

Cybersecurity is frequently viewed as a technical responsibility assigned to an IT department or external service provider. However, its implications extend directly to business growth, financial stability and customer trust.

As organizations expand, they typically collect more customer information, process larger transaction volumes and provide system access to additional employees and partners. Each expansion can introduce new security considerations.

Weak access controls, outdated applications, inadequate backup procedures and insufficient employee training may increase exposure to cyber threats.

A serious security incident can interrupt operations, damage customer relationships and create substantial recovery expenses. For smaller businesses, the financial and operational consequences can be particularly difficult to absorb.

Effective cybersecurity requires more than installing security software. Organizations should implement appropriate access controls, maintain reliable backups, regularly update systems and establish procedures for responding to incidents.

Employee awareness is equally important because human mistakes can undermine otherwise effective technical safeguards.

Business leaders should consider cybersecurity investments part of their overall risk-management strategy. Protecting systems and information helps maintain the operational stability necessary for sustainable expansion.

Modern businesses generate significant amounts of information through sales transactions, marketing campaigns, customer interactions and internal operations. Yet collecting data does not automatically translate into better decisions.

Many organizations struggle with inconsistent reporting, duplicated records, outdated information and fragmented data sources.

For example, a company might report strong revenue growth while overlooking increasing customer acquisition costs or declining profitability. Similarly, managers may make inventory decisions using incomplete information because different departments maintain separate records.

These challenges can become more serious as organizations expand into additional markets or introduce new products.

A reliable data strategy begins with establishing consistent definitions for important business metrics. Teams should agree on how revenue, customer retention, operational efficiency and other key indicators are measured. Organizations should also identify the systems responsible for maintaining authoritative records.

Automated reporting can reduce manual errors, while regular data-quality reviews help identify inconsistencies before they affect important decisions.

Ultimately, entrepreneurs need information that is accurate, accessible and relevant to their strategic priorities. The goal is not to collect as much data as possible but to turn reliable information into timely business decisions.

Rapid growth creates exciting opportunities, but it also places additional pressure on existing business systems.

A technology setup designed for a company with 10 employees may not adequately support an organization with hundreds of employees operating across multiple locations.

Increased transaction volumes, additional users, more complex reporting requirements and greater customer expectations can expose previously unnoticed limitations.

Businesses may experience application slowdowns, service interruptions, inconsistent processes or rising infrastructure expenses. These problems often emerge when organizations expand faster than their technology planning. Scalability should therefore be considered before major expansion initiatives.

Business leaders can begin by evaluating whether existing systems can accommodate increased workloads and additional users. They should also examine whether infrastructure can be upgraded without requiring expensive or disruptive changes.

Cloud services, modular software architecture and well-documented operational processes may provide greater flexibility, depending on the organization’s requirements. However, scalability involves people and processes as much as technology.

Planning ahead can help companies avoid reactive technology investments made under pressure.

Even the most advanced technology cannot deliver its full potential if employees do not understand how to use it effectively.

Businesses sometimes invest substantial resources in software implementation while allocating limited time or budget to training.

This can lead to inconsistent adoption, employee frustration and continued dependence on inefficient manual processes. In some cases, employees may avoid using new systems altogether because they find familiar workflows easier.

Successful technology adoption requires clear communication about why changes are being introduced and how they will benefit daily operations. Employees should receive practical training relevant to their responsibilities.

Organizations can also identify internal technology champions who help colleagues understand new processes and provide feedback during implementation. Regular evaluations can reveal whether systems are being used as intended and whether additional training is required.

By treating employee development as part of technology investment, businesses can improve adoption rates and achieve more consistent operational benefits.

One of the most common strategic mistakes is approaching technology decisions individually rather than as part of a coordinated plan.

A business might replace an application when it fails, upgrade infrastructure when performance deteriorates or introduce new software when a department requests additional capabilities. While these decisions may solve immediate problems, they can create a fragmented technology environment over time.

A long-term technology roadmap provides a more structured approach.

It should identify current infrastructure limitations, anticipated business requirements, implementation priorities and realistic investment timelines. Business leaders should collaborate with technical specialists to evaluate which systems require immediate attention and which can be improved gradually.

The roadmap should also account for potential changes in customer demand, staffing, regulatory requirements and market conditions. Regular reviews are important because business priorities and technology capabilities continue to evolve.

A useful roadmap does not need to predict every future requirement. Instead, it should provide a flexible framework for making informed decisions while minimizing unnecessary disruption.

Technology problems often remain hidden until they begin affecting revenue, productivity or customer satisfaction. By that stage, addressing them may require urgent investments and operational changes that could have been avoided through earlier planning.

Entrepreneurs can take a more proactive approach by reviewing their technology environment regularly and identifying potential weaknesses before they become significant obstacles. This includes evaluating outdated systems, improving application integration, monitoring database performance, strengthening cybersecurity and investing in employee training.

Equally important is connecting every major technology decision to a measurable business objective. Not every company needs the newest software, the most sophisticated infrastructure or an immediate migration to emerging technologies. In many cases, improving existing systems and simplifying workflows can produce meaningful results without unnecessary spending.

The businesses best positioned for sustainable growth are not necessarily those investing the most in technology. They are those making thoughtful decisions about where technology can deliver lasting operational and strategic value.

Ultimately, business growth depends on more than ambitious goals and market opportunities. It also requires a reliable foundation capable of supporting those ambitions.

By recognizing and addressing hidden technology challenges early, entrepreneurs can reduce operational friction, make better decisions and create organizations that are better prepared for the next stage of growth.

For most entrepreneurs, growth is the ultimate measure of success. Expanding into new markets, acquiring customers, increasing revenue and building stronger teams are often the priorities that dominate strategic discussions.

However, one critical factor frequently receives less attention: the technology infrastructure supporting everyday business operations.

A company might have an excellent product, a growing customer base and an ambitious expansion strategy, yet still struggle to scale because its internal systems cannot keep up with increasing demand.

#5496. PicoBrew’s patents are back on the market, six years after the Seattle homebrew startup’s collapse

Chronicling the Seattle and Pacific Northwest startup scene. SEE MORE

by Kurt Schlosser on Oct 28, 2026 at 10:36 amOctober 28, 2026 at 3:08 pm

The patents behind PicoBrew, the Seattle startup that once promised to do for home beer what Keurig did for coffee, are up for sale again — six years after the company collapsed into receivership and after two changes of ownership.

Hilco Global, an Illinois-based diversified financial services company, announced this week that its Intellectual Property Services group has been retained by PicoBrew’s current owner to market the startup’s technology to potential buyers.

The sale includes 17 patents and patent applications, two of them pending, along with engineering and design files and product concepts. Buyers can bid on all or part of the portfolio, and non-binding indications of interest are due Nov. 18. Hilco is pitching the assets to companies in coffee, tea, kombucha, spirits, beverage appliances and housewares.

The seller is Pico Craft Group, which Hilco described as led by a former PicoBrew investor. After PicoBrew’s 2020 collapse, its bridge lender took over the assets. That lender, PB Funding Group, was managed by former Microsoft software developer Greg Whitten, The Seattle Times reported at the time. Pico Craft Group bought the assets from the lender in 2024 for an undisclosed amount, according to Hilco, which did not say who runs the group.

“PicoBrew was a true innovator in the consumer and commercial craft beverage space, and its portfolio has applications well beyond beer,” Eric Hurwitz, a senior director at Hilco, said in a news release.

The portfolio covers technology from PicoBrew’s full product line, according to the release, including the Pico Pro and Pico C home brewing appliances, the PicoStill accessory for spirits, the Pico U Multibrew platform for beer, coffee, tea and kombucha, and Z-Series brewing machines and KegSmarts kegerators for commercial use.

Bill Mitchell, a former Microsoft vice president and longtime homebrewer, founded PicoBrew in 2010 with his brother Jim Mitchell, a food scientist, and Avi Geiger, an engineer who also worked at Microsoft. Their countertop machines automated the brewing process using PicoPaks, ingredient packs based on recipes from craft breweries.

The startup became a Kickstarter regular. Its 2017 campaign for the Pico Model C raised $1.93 million from 4,301 backers, a record at the time in the site’s food category, and the $549 machine landed at retailers including Best Buy, Williams-Sonoma and Amazon. A 2018 campaign for the Pico U pushed PicoBrew into coffee, tea and kombucha.

But the company struggled to land more funding. In February 2020, after failing to close a new round, PicoBrew entered receivership. It had raised more than $15 million and cut its staff to fewer than 40, down from a peak of more than 80.

PicoBrew ceased operations in 2020, and no one has supported existing devices since, according to Hilco. Any decision about future support would be up to a buyer. The King County Superior Court approved the 2020 sale, which freed PicoBrew’s bridge lender from the company’s liabilities and from responsibility to past customers, The Seattle Times previously reported.

Some owners kept their machines brewing without the company’s servers by using a workaround developed by a Facebook group of PicoBrew users, The Spoon reported in 2020. The founders were let go after the receivership, according to the site.

When PicoBrew went up for sale in 2020, Mitchell told GeekWire that hardware takes time and multiple funding rounds backed by firm investor commitment.

He shared advice he’d gotten from Dan Leviton of Maveron: “Startups only fail for one of two reasons — they run out of heart, or they run out of money.”

#5495. Current price of oil as of November 2, 2026

As of 6:30 a.m. Eastern Time today, oil sold for $112.60 per barrel (using Brent as the benchmark, which we’ll get into momentarily). That’s $3.26 lower than yesterday morning and approximately a $47 rise over the past year.

It’s impossible to predict the future of oil prices. Several factors determine the movement of oil, but it ultimately boils down to supply and demand. Again, when threats of economic downturn, war, etc. are high, the oil trajectory can turn rapidly.

When you pay for gas at the pump, you’re paying for more than just the crude oil itself; you’re also springing for links along the chain, such as the refineries and wholesalers—not to mention taxes and local gas station markups.

Still, the crude oil aspect affects the final price most dramatically, as it typically accounts for more than half the price per gallon. When oil prices spike, so do gas prices. And frustratingly, when oil prices drop, gas prices tend to take their time drifting down to the lower price (sometimes referred to as “rockets and feathers”).

In case of emergency, the U.S. has a store of crude oil known as the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. Its primary purpose is energy security in case of disaster (think sanctions, severe storm damage, even war). But it can also go a long way toward softening crippling price hikes during supply shocks.

It’s not a long-term answer—more of an immediate relief to assist the consumer and keep critical parts of the economy running, like key industries, emergency services, public transportation, etc.

Oil and natural gas are both major energy fuels. A big change in oil prices can affect natural gas by extension. For example, if oil prices increase, some industries may swap natural gas for some segments of their operations where possible—which increases demand for natural gas.

When examining oil’s performance, there are generally two major benchmarks:

Between the two, Brent better represents global oil performance because it prices much of the world’s traded crude. And, it’s often the best way to track historical oil performance. In fact, even the U.S. Energy Information Administration now uses Brent as its primary reference in its Annual Energy Outlook.

Looking at the Brent benchmark across several decades, oil has been anything but steady. It’s seen spikes due to factors such as wars and supply cuts, and it’s also seen crashes from global recessions and an oversupply (called a “glut”). For example:

All to say, oil’s historical performance has been anything but smooth. Again, it’s hugely affected by wars, recessions, OPEC whims, evolving energy initiatives and policies, and much more.

Looking to stay up-to-date regarding the latest energy developments? Check out our recent coverage:

The current price of oil per barrel depends largely on supply and demand, including news about potential future supply and demand (geopolitics, decisions made by OPEC+, etc.). In the U.S., prices also move based on how friendly an administration is to drilling, as it can affect future supply. For example, 2025 saw the Trump administration move to reopen more than 1.5 million acres in the Coastal Plain of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge for oil and gas leasing, reversing the Biden administration’s policy of limiting oil drilling in the Arctic.

The price of oil updates constantly when the “futures” markets are open. A futures market is effectively an auction where people agree to buy or sell oil in the future. As long as people and companies are trading contracts, the oil price is changing.

In short, shale is rock that contains oil and natural gas. Think of shale as energy yet to be tapped. The more shale the U.S. accesses, the more energy we’ll have—and the more easily oil prices can keep from spiking as much thanks to a greater supply.

When oil is expensive, it tends to make everyday items cost more. This can be related to energy (your heating, gas utilities, etc.), but it’s also due to the logistics involved with making those items accessible to you. Shipping, for example, can affect the price of things at the grocery store, as it’s more expensive to get those products from warehouses and farms onto the shelf.
